title: LLMs to Support K–12 Teachers in Culturally Relevant Pedagogy: An AI Literacy Example
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether a large language model (LLM)-based tool can help K–12 teachers implement culturally relevant pedagogy (CRP) when adapting AI literacy lessons. The authors argue that although CRP is associated with improved student engagement and achievement, teachers often struggle to apply it because of time constraints, limited training, and lack of resources. At the same time, AI literacy is emerging in K–12 education, but available materials are rarely tailored to students’ cultural and demographic contexts. The study asks how an LLM-supported tool influences teachers’ ability to design culturally responsive AI literacy activities and what strengths and opportunities teachers perceive in such a tool.

The intervention studied is CulturAIEd, an LLM-powered system designed to help teachers adapt AI literacy activities using CRP/CRT principles. The tool incorporates student demographic information, offers basic and advanced lesson modifications, uses a culturally responsive teaching checklist, provides rubric-based scoring and formative feedback, and includes a chatbot for just-in-time pedagogical support. The pilot procedure involved 90–120 minute one-on-one Zoom sessions with a pre-survey, multiple lesson adaptation tasks, post-survey, and interview. Teachers first designed or adapted AI literacy activities without guidance, then with a CRT checklist, and finally with CulturAIEd. Participants could also use other generative AI tools and online resources during the session.

The population consisted of four secondary teachers teaching grades 9–12, with three recruited from North America and one from East Asia. Contexts included public schools and one virtual public school. The focus was on teachers as the direct users of the tool, but the intended instructional context was high school AI literacy learning for students. Data analysis was described as qualitative-dominant mixed methods, using thematic analysis of interviews plus descriptive analysis of survey responses.

The main conclusion is that CulturAIEd showed promise for increasing teachers’ confidence and perceived efficiency in integrating culturally responsive elements into AI literacy activities. Participants valued the tool’s demographic integration, actionable feedback, and rubric structure, and post-survey ratings suggested increased confidence in identifying opportunities for cultural responsiveness. However, the authors emphasize that this was a preliminary exploratory pilot, not conclusive evidence of effectiveness. They note important risks such as LLM bias, stereotyping, and over-reliance on AI, and call for larger, controlled, longitudinal studies to examine impacts on teacher practice and student outcomes more rigorously.

identified_tools.name: CulturAIEd
identified_tools.description: An LLM-powered teacher-support system designed to help K-12 teachers adapt AI literacy activities using culturally relevant/responsive pedagogy principles. It integrates student demographic information, CRT checklist-based modification guidance, rubric-based scoring, formative feedback, and a just-in-time chatbot for pedagogical support.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a prototype tool used by four K-12 teachers to adapt AI literacy lessons to students' cultural contexts and to support culturally responsive lesson planning.

findings.finding_summary: In an exploratory pilot with four K-12 teachers, participants reported that CulturAIEd streamlined CRP integration and was viewed as highly efficient for adapting AI literacy activities. Post-survey results indicated that 3/4 participants strongly agreed the tool saved time and inspired new ideas, though no effect size or inferential statistics were reported.
findings.measure: Teacher post-survey perceptions of time-saving and idea generation

findings.finding_summary: All four participants reported increased confidence in implementing culturally responsive modifications after using CulturAIEd. Confidence in identifying opportunities for cultural responsiveness rose from pre-survey ratings of 3-5 to all participants rating 5/5 on the post-survey, based on descriptive survey results and interviews.
findings.measure: Teacher self-reported confidence in identifying opportunities for cultural responsiveness in learning activities

findings.finding_summary: Interview findings indicated that teachers perceived CulturAIEd as helpful for making culturally responsive modifications to existing activities, with participants valuing its actionable feedback, rubric feature, and integrated demographic customization. The paper frames these as promising trends from qualitative data rather than conclusive evidence of efficacy.
findings.measure: Teacher interview perceptions of pedagogical support for culturally responsive lesson adaptation

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot based on GPT-family large language models.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned as a generative AI tool that participants could access during lesson adaptation tasks and reported using in their broader teaching practice for lesson planning, simplifying texts, and generating examples; it was not the focal intervention evaluated in the study.

identified_tools.name: Turnitin
identified_tools.description: A plagiarism detection and writing assessment platform used in education.
identified_tools.use_case: Mentioned in survey responses as an AI-related tool teachers actively use; not evaluated as the intervention in this study.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot based on GPT-family large language models.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as the underlying model family for the CulturAIEd demo via gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18.

quality_tier_rationale: This is an exploratory qualitative-dominant mixed-methods pilot with a very small sample (n=4) and descriptive pre/post survey results only. The authors explicitly state the findings are not generalizable and should be interpreted as promising trends rather than rigorous efficacy evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported outcomes are positive but based on self-reported confidence, satisfaction, and perceived efficiency without effect sizes or validated impact estimates. The direction is promising, but the magnitude of impact is unclear.
